description: An offline AI-powered desk companion robot unit that translates natural language commands using a local LLM into motor movements and eye/face animations on an ESP32 via WebSockets, with camera vision enabled by an ESP32-CAM.

chat.py.purpose: Main interactive shell loop running a local Ollama LLM instance (qwen2.5:3b). Interprets user requests, generates formatted JSON responses, parses inline emotion tags and movement tool calls, injects dynamic camera visual context, and dispatches them to robot.py.

functions.name: parse_segments
outputs: list of (emotion: str, text: str) tuples
functions.description: Splits a response string containing inline [emotion] tags into individual segments for display on the OLED.

vision.py.purpose: Decodes HTTP MJPEG streams from ESP32-CAM and runs thread-safe background face detection (Haar Cascade) and object detection (MobileNet-SSD).

VisionSystem.description: Handles stream reading, OpenCV image processing, and bounding box rendering.

methods.name: __init__
methods.description: Initializes OpenCV classifiers and DNN parameters.

methods.name: stop
methods.description: Shuts down background thread and destroys windows.

methods.name: get_latest_detections
methods.description: Thread-safe retrieval of face count and detected object labels.

robot.py.purpose: WebSocket controller client that provides a Python API to send movement, emotion, and text display commands directly to the ESP32 WebSocket server.

Robot.description: Encapsulates the WebSocket connection and command sending methods.

methods.name: __init__
methods.description: Establishes a WebSocket connection to the ESP32 at ws://{ip}:81.

methods.name: send
methods.description: Sends a plain text command to the ESP32 and prints the acknowledgement reply.

methods.name: forward
methods.description: Sends FORWARD command to ESP32. Stops after duration if duration > 0.

methods.name: backward
methods.description: Sends BACKWARD command to ESP32. Stops after duration if duration > 0.

methods.name: left
methods.description: Sends LEFT command to ESP32 (pivot left). Stops after duration if duration > 0.

methods.name: right
methods.description: Sends RIGHT command to ESP32 (pivot right). Stops after duration if duration > 0.

methods.name: stop
methods.description: Sends STOP command to ESP32 (coasts motors).

methods.name: display
methods.description: Sends DISPLAY:<text> to display text on OLED.

methods.name: display_open
methods.description: Sends DISPLAY_OPEN command to open speech box on OLED.

methods.name: display_close
methods.description: Sends DISPLAY_CLOSE command to close speech box and return to eye animations.

methods.name: dance
methods.description: Runs a pre-defined sequence of movements and emotion/expression commands.

methods.name: sing
methods.description: Sways left/right, changes emotions, and displays musical note symbols on the screen.

test_robot.py.purpose: A diagnostics script to test raw WebSocket connections and direct DISPLAY commands.

test_socket.py.purpose: A diagnostics script to test TCP connectivity to the ESP32 on port 81.

esp32_controller.ino.purpose: Main body firmware file that runs a WebSocket server on port 81, parses incoming commands, controls L293D motor driver GPIOs, handles speech scroll on SSD1306 OLED, and coordinates eye rendering.

functions.name: parseCommand
functions.description: Parses commands for OLED display control, 18 emotions, and 5 motor movements.

functions.name: prepareMessage
functions.description: Wraps input text to fit the 75px wide OLED speech box boundaries without splitting words.

functions.name: updateSpeechScroll
functions.description: Updates animations for speech box opening, text scrolling, and speech box closing.

functions.name: drawSpeakingText
functions.description: Draws speech box frame and lines of text inside the visible box area.

functions.name: moveForward
functions.description: Sets L293D GPIOs for forward motion.

functions.name: moveBackward
functions.description: Sets L293D GPIOs for backward motion.

functions.name: moveLeft
functions.description: Sets L293D GPIOs for left pivot spin.

functions.name: moveRight
functions.description: Sets L293D GPIOs for right pivot spin.

functions.name: stopMotors
functions.description: Disables motor enable pins to stop movements.

esp32_cam.ino.purpose: ESP32-CAM firmware that captures OV2640 frames and hosts low-latency MJPEG video streaming server on port 80.

functions.name: index_handler
functions.description: Serves responsive HTML stream viewer page.

functions.name: capture_handler
functions.description: Captures and serves a single JPEG snapshot.

functions.name: stream_handler
functions.description: Streams continuous JPEG images as multipart/x-mixed-replace MJPEG feed.

esp32-eyes.purpose: A dynamic eye animation library using U8g2.

components.Face: Manages face state, active expressions, and blink timers.
components.Eye: Encapsulates size, position, scale, and interpolation for a single eye.
components.FaceExpression: Implements transition logic for 18 custom expressions (Normal, Happy, Focused, etc.).
components.EyeDrawer: Handles low-level rendering shapes on SSD1306 OLED screen.
components.Animations: Interpolates scaling and coordinate changes smoothly over frames.
